name: fragment-varying-float4-passthrough
rationale: The fragment entry returns its perspective center float4 varying unchanged; the shared generated fullscreen vertex stage supplies the declared varying and the selected RGBA32Float pixel captures interpolation byte-exactly.

name: fragment-varying-float-to-half
rationale: The fragment entry truncates its perspective center scalar float varying to half and writes color location zero; the shared generated fullscreen vertex stage supplies the varying and the selected R16Float pixel captures the conversion byte-exactly.

name: fragment-position-depth
rationale: The fragment entry extracts the z lane of its center no-perspective position builtin and writes that scalar to a one-pixel R32Float target, capturing the generated full-screen draw depth exactly.

name: unfold-a-padded-two-by-two-window-over-a-three-by-three-bfloat-image
rationale: MLX's naive convolution unfold: each thread computes one output element of the im2col matrix by walking the two spatial axes backwards, accumulating an output offset and an input coordinate per axis, and copies one bfloat -- or writes zero when the coordinate falls in the padding. It is the shape `native/emitter/body/reinterpret_pointer.rs::local_alloca_storage_compatible` keys on: the per-axis coordinates are spilled into a single `alloca i64` that the second loop reads back as `[2 x i32]`, so an eight-byte local is addressed as two four-byte elements. 91 corpus modules reach that rule and no authored case did; this is one of the smallest at 230 lines. The parameters are a 3x3 single-channel image, a 2x2 window, stride 1, padding 1, both dilations 1, and the flip flag clear, so the 4x4 grid writes sixteen distinct output elements: nine copy an input value and seven land in the padding and must be exactly +0. Every value is a small integer float, exact in bfloat's eight mantissa bits, and the kernel only copies -- it never computes in floating point -- so the answer does not depend on rounding or on fast-math association. Every params byte outside the fields listed above is 0xCC, including wt_strides and out_strides, which this entry never reads. `authored_bounded`: all four loops are two-iteration loops whose trip count is a compile-time constant -- three alternate an `i1` phi from true to false, the fourth counts an `i32` phi down from 1 -- so no input can change how many times any of them runs.

name: dynamic-texel-offsets-outside-metals-range-on-a-sample-and-a-gather
rationale: What Apple GPUs return for dynamic texel offsets outside Metal's documented range (the L7d handback on DESIGN D102.3). MSL 6.13 says the offset of sample and gather must be in [-8, 7] and states no result outside it; D102 clamps a dynamic offset into [-8, 7] before Vulkan's Offset operand, so this reading shows whether the device clamps too (8 behaves as 7), wraps to a narrow two's-complement field (8 behaves as -8 in four bits; 16 as 0; 32 as 0 in five), or applies the value unchanged (8 moves eight texels). This is a probe of behaviour outside Metal's contract, recorded as a Metal observation; a Vulkan result that differs here is a finding for WP-L7d's clamp, not by itself a translation defect. The offsets, one per lane, are (8, 0), (0, 8), (-9, 0), (0, -9), (8, 7), (-8, -9), (15, -16), (16, 0), (0, -16), (-17, 17), (24, -24), (31, -32), (100, -100), (-128, 127), (255, -256), (2147483647, -2147483648). The kernel samples a 64x64 r32_float texture whose texel (x, y) holds x + 64y (exact binary32) at the centre of texel (32, 32), normalized (32.5/64, 32.5/64), through a constexpr nearest, clamp_to_edge sampler: lane t reads int2 offset o from buffer 0 and writes t.sample(s, uv, level(0), o) to out[2t] and t.gather(s, uv, o) (component x) to out[2t+1] of buffer 1. The sample returns the texel at (32 + o.x, 32 + o.y) clamped to the texture, so its value names the offset the device applied (x = value mod 64, y = value div 64, readable for every applied offset in [-32, 31]); the gather returns the x components of its 2x2 footprint, texels 32 + o.x .. 33 + o.x by 32 + o.y .. 33 + o.y, each clamped, in the gather's component order (Vulkan's is (i0, j1), (i1, j1), (i1, j0), (i0, j0)). The output is pre-filled with 0xAB so an unwritten slot is visible; each lane writes only its own two float4s; the AIR has no loop.

name: dynamic-texel-offsets-within-metals-range-on-a-sample-and-a-gather
rationale: Texel values of dynamic texel offsets inside Metal's range (the L7d handback: A/B evidence for DESIGN D102, which lowers a dynamic offset on a sample as the Offset operand of SClamp(offset, -8, 7) where the device has maintenance8, and on a gather as the same clamped Offset). MSL 6.13 requires the offset of sample and gather in [-8, 7]; every offset here is, so the clamp is the identity and the Vulkan result must equal Metal's exactly. The offsets, one per lane, are (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (-1, -1), (7, 7), (-8, -8), (7, -8), (-8, 7), (3, -5), (-6, 2), (5, 5), (-3, 4), (2, -7), (-7, 6), (6, -1), (-2, -3). The kernel samples a 64x64 r32_float texture whose texel (x, y) holds x + 64y (exact binary32) at the centre of texel (32, 32), normalized (32.5/64, 32.5/64), through a constexpr nearest, clamp_to_edge sampler: lane t reads int2 offset o from buffer 0 and writes t.sample(s, uv, level(0), o) to out[2t] and t.gather(s, uv, o) (component x) to out[2t+1] of buffer 1. The sample returns the texel at (32 + o.x, 32 + o.y) clamped to the texture, so its value names the offset the device applied (x = value mod 64, y = value div 64, readable for every applied offset in [-32, 31]); the gather returns the x components of its 2x2 footprint, texels 32 + o.x .. 33 + o.x by 32 + o.y .. 33 + o.y, each clamped, in the gather's component order (Vulkan's is (i0, j1), (i1, j1), (i1, j0), (i0, j0)). name: linked-k48-quantized-matrix-multiply-float-16-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes (1 simdgroup) runs the single 16x16 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 16, K = 48, so the tile is full in M and N (the unsafe loader path) and K runs one whole 32-deep block and a 16-deep remainder (the safe loader). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48) and every row holds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, so every row of the result is the same: the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 16 words observed (offset 0, 64 bytes) do not depend on write order. W[n][k] (row stride w_ld = 48 bytes) holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (all 16 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads) and a column computed from another column's weights changes its word; scales and biases (scales_ld = biases_ld = 1, sized N*K) repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and 0, 1, 2, 3 (biases unread without the bias bit). Each dequantized weight is q * s, a multiple of 0.5 at most 30, exact in float and in the threadgroup tile; each product with x is a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction, and on the float inputs.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-matrix-multiply
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: A one-thread zero-extent quantized matrix-multiply invocation keeps every loop bound finite and observes the four-byte destination allocation. The two AIR direct visible references use globally retained modules with matching ABI signatures. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: scale-a-skybox-texel-by-two-in-range-flags-and-a-half-mix
rationale: The fragment samples one texel of a texture2d_array, then folds two bool2 range tests -- is the texture coordinate at or above zero, is it at or below one -- into floats and multiplies the four flags together into a single in-range scalar. That scalar is mixed against one with the buffer's third float as the weight, so the weight is what makes the flags observable: at a weight of one half a convert that answered zero instead of one would halve the result, writing 0.0625, 0.125, 0.1875 and 0.25 where the correct flags write 0.125, 0.25, 0.375 and 0.5. The writeSRGB function constant is set false so the straight path is taken and the alpha lane is the saturate of an already in-range half. Every value is exactly representable in half and the mix reduces to one plus zero, so nothing here depends on rounding.

name: linked-single-unit-sdpa-fwd-new
rationale: One 32-thread threadgroup, a single simdgroup, runs the float path: function constant 115 is 1, so srcDataType is 0, every feature flag is off, simd sums are emulated through threadgroup buffer 5 (128 bytes, one float per lane), and the context unroll factor is 1. Function constant 122 is 3, so the buffers table has three slots: element 0 holds zeros (query, key, and mask, at qIndex, kIndex, and mIndex 0), element 2 holds the value 0.75 (vIndex 2), and the linked postfix writes the result to element 1. Every extent, count, and stride is one and the scale index is negative, so no scale-array dereference occurs. Every divisor on the path is one (the head and KV-group divisions and the context remainder by the unroll factor) and every shift amount is a constant below the width. Every loop has a literal bound and a step of at least one: the zeroing, context-block, feature, unroll, and simdgroup-merge loops run once each, and the emulated reduction tree halves the 32-lane width down to stride one. Every lane's score is zero, so every lane stores the same row maximum 0 and row sum 1, softmax gives the single key weight one, and lane 0 writes the value 0.75.

name: linked-k48-quantized-matrix-multiply-bfloat-64-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. name: linked-zero-k-quantized-matrix-multiply-bfloat
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.

name: narrow-one-premultiplied-tap-past-a-byte-three-different-ways
rationale: A five-by-five weighted downsample over a one-by-one source keeps exactly the centre tap, so the whole stencil reduces to one uchar4 scaled by one weight. The kernel then divides the premultiplied accumulator by its own alpha, scales by 255, truncates to uint4 and narrows that to uchar4. The three colour lanes were chosen so the uint4 is 187, 1342 and 536: one lane fits a byte and two do not, so a narrowing that saturated instead of truncating would write 255 where the truncation writes 62 and 24. Every lane, including the alpha lane that structurally reduces to 255, gives the same truncated integer under the accumulator ordering as written, under the ordering with the weight cancelled, under a folded reciprocal and in double precision, so fast-math reassociation cannot move the result.

name: ulong-texture-atomic-max-reads-and-writes-on-one-2d-texture
rationale: unk_ulong_atomic_rw, a ulong texture read, updated atomically, and written in one function beside one only read and written (D283 family D): texture 0 (a) and 1 (b) are read_write 2D rg32_uint 8 x 2 holding random 64-bit texels (low word in R). 12 threads in one threadgroup, k = 0xF00D0000C0DE0000 + t: thread t reads a at (t, 0) and writes it to out[2t] of buffer 0 (ulong4 elements, pre-filled with 0xAB), applies atomic_max of (read.x ^ k) to a at (t & 7, 1) (threads t and t + 8 share a texel; the maxima commute), writes ulong4(read.x + 1, 2, 3, 4) to a at (t, 0), then reads b at (t, 0), writes it to out[2t + 1], and writes ulong4(read.x ^ k, 5, 6, 7) to b at (t, 0). Threads 8 to 11 read and write past both widths: Metal reads (0, 0, 0, 1) and writes nothing there. Texture a is the atomic slot (the binder's R64_UINT view), b the RG32 one. Both textures are out-of-bounds targets. The AIR has no loop. Observed: texture 0 (the atomically updated texture), whole, after the work.

name: ulong-texture-atomic-min-and-max-on-a-1d-array-texture
rationale: unk_ulong_atomics, the atomic_max and atomic_min of Metal's ulong textures (D283 family D), which compare unsigned 64-bit texels and return nothing, each texture rg32_uint holding random 64-bit texels (low word in R, the top bit varying): texture 0 a read_write 1D 16 wide, 1 a 1D array 16 x 2 layers, 2 a 2D 16 x 2 (16-bit coordinates), 3 a 2D array 16 x 2 x 2 layers, 4 a 3D 16 x 2 x 2, 5 a texture buffer 16 texels. 80 threads in threadgroups of 16: thread t updates texel x = t & 15 (plus 16 from thread 64, past every width, where Metal changes nothing) at y = t >> 4 & 1 as row, layer, and slice (the 3D at (x, y, y)) with v = t * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 (mod 2^64; its top bit varies): atomic_max where x < 8, atomic_min elsewhere, so each texel takes one operation from two threads (four in the 1D and buffer textures, which ignore y), from different threadgroups, and the operations commute. Every texture is an out-of-bounds target; the texture buffer's 128-byte guard covers texels 16 to 31. The AIR has no loop. Observed: texture 1 (1D array), whole, after the atomics.

name: linked-single-unit-scan-mul
rationale: One invocation and one thread execute one scan element with unit source, destination, and intermediate extents. Every loop bound and elements-per-thread field is one, the axis is zero, and the four-byte threadgroup allocation holds the single float lane before one exact destination write.

name: linked-single-invocation-zero-bin
rationale: One invocation is bounded by source_size 1x1. Linking is enabled with one authored texture and one address-table element; the exact callback is loop-free and returns float4 zero without dereferencing either resource. The one-bin histogram parameters force every active scalar lane to bin zero, and the poisoned counter makes the bounded global-atomic write observable byte-exactly.

name: a14-nhwc-bfloat-2x2-kernel-six-by-five-channels-two-images
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-extent case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC). Constant 89 = 0x56 states C mod 16 = 6 and O mod 16 = 5 and selects no linking, no reduction, not 1x1 and not the 16x16 multiply (bit 17 clear); constant 124 = 0x101b607 selects unit stride, unit dilation, one group, NHWC (bit 26 clear), tiles O = C = K = 8, one k-split and one simdgroup per threadgroup, both tiles in registers (no threadgroup staging), the image edge check, and C and O not multiples of their tiles. So the entry takes the A14 NHWC kernel, which multiplies bfloat 8x8 simdgroup matrices into float accumulators, each lane building its two fragment cells from its lane index (the device-measured layout: row ((L >> 1) & 3) | ((L >> 4) << 2), columns ((L >> 3) & 1) 4 + (L & 1) 2 and the next). The 448-byte parameters (binding 26): 6 input and 5 output channels, a 2 x 2 kernel, batch 2 in one sub-batch, a 5 x 2 source and a 5 x 2 gradient, offsets (-1, 0), 10 gradient positions per image (one full 8-position chunk and a 2-position tail), 16-bit magic divisors 2 (kW, kH) and 5 (gradient width) and the 32-bit divisor 5, uber tiles 1, per-image element counts 50 and 60, weightsOutputChannels 5, numWeights 120. Four threadgroups of 32 threads, threadgroup x = ky 2 + kx, each compute dW[ky][kx][c][o] = sum over n, gy, gx of gradient[n][gy][gx][o] source[n][gy + ky][gx + kx - 1][c], loading zero for positions left of the source, channels past 6 and output channels past 5, and store it to destination word ((ky 2 + kx) 6 + c) 5 + o (HWIO; binding 27, poisoned 0xab, all 120 words written). Every source and gradient value is one of [-3.5, -3.0, -2.5, -2.0, -1.5, -1.0, -0.5, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 5.0], exact in bfloat (exponents where both 8-bit conventions agree): source element i takes entry (7i + 3) mod 16, gradient element i entry (3i + 5) mod 16. Every product is a multiple of 1/4 of magnitude at most 25 and every sum (at most 20 terms) lies in [-35.75, 51.0], so every word is exact in any summation order; no output is zero. Loops are bounded by the two images, the two chunks per image and the fixed tile counts.

name: linked-zero-work-bfloat-convolution-weight-gradient
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The selected static tile configuration keeps derived divisors nonzero. Zero gradient parameters give the sole invocation no output-channel or spatial work, reaching the bounds exit before resource or linked-function writes and preserving the poisoned destination. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-three-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 and 3 and receives exact float4 zero from both linked _uber_clear bodies. A five-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected as the result. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before its subgroup aggregation path, and binding zero is selected byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-seven-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 7 and receives exact float4 zero from all six linked _uber_clear bodies. rationale: Eight threads (DESIGN D225, the texel buffer form; Metal defines the results: a read out of bounds returns zero, a write out of bounds is ignored, so the case compares with Metal). src and dst are 4-texel r32_uint texture buffers. name: five-fast-float3-transcendentals-off-the-anchors
rationale:
fast::log2, fast::log, fast::exp2, fast::rsqrt and fast::sin on float3, 95 corpus sources between them and none of them reached by any corpus host. Three arguments each, chosen off the exactly-representable anchors on purpose: 1.0000001, 12345.678 and 1e-30 for log2; 0.36787945, 1234567 and 6.02e23 for log; 0.5, -17.375 and 23.71 for exp2; 134404, 3.7 and 1e-20 for rsqrt; and 0.7853982, 100 and -3.14159 for sin. Large mantissas and mixed exponents are the point: a case built only on powers of two would agree with an implementation that is wrong everywhere else, and 134404 in particular is the one rsqrt argument this repository has already measured the hardware to miss by an ulp.

Every one of the fifteen expected values was derived in float64 and rounded once to float32, and every one of the fifteen observations is within 2 ULP of that -- so the case asserts Metal's approximation, which is what a fast_ intrinsic promises, rather than correct rounding, which it does not. That tolerance is far too tight to hide a substituted function: log for log2 or sqrt for rsqrt moves these arguments by whole factors, not by two units in the last place.

The second sine argument, 100, is also the argument that caught the argument reduction this translator used to emit ahead of every fast trig call, where it came back 38 ULP out.

name: quantized-tile-8x8x8-float-q-int8-kv-one-row-64-keys
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-parameter case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of two simdgroups: queryLength 1 (only row 0 reaches the callback; the seven padding rows of the 8-row tile read zero queries and an all-zero mask, finite, never written), contextLength 64 = two 32-key context tiles, so the first tile's normalized result goes through the O-sum workspace (binding 27) and is rescaled into the second; dimsPerHead 32 = paddedDimsPerHead, alpha 0.5. Row 0's query is (4, 1, -1, 1, 0, ...); the four attended keys 5, 22, 40, 57 (two per tile) carry int8 codes of (120, 8, -4, 12) under scales 1, 2 or 4, so they dequantize to the same vector and score the row maximum 252; every other key scores at least 150 below, and the keys of the attended pattern at n mod 7 = 3 are removed by the mask (-1000). Every softmax weight is 0 or exp(0) = 1, the running sums are 2 then 4, the rescale between tiles is exp(0) = 1, and each output is the mean of four int8 values times power-of-two scales (multiples of 1/16), exact. name: channel-norm-raises-an-exact-one-to-a-fractional-power
rationale: The largest uncovered symbol needs a base whose logarithm is exact, and only one is: powr(1, y) is one for every implementation, because exp2(y * log2(1)) is exp2(0) whatever polynomial computes log2. The params buffer sets alpha to zero and delta to one, so the base is exactly one in all four lanes whatever the sampled texel squares to, and the result is the texel itself scaled by one. The struct offsets are load-bearing rather than the arithmetic: alpha sits at byte 0 and delta at byte 8, so reading them from each others slots makes the base the squared texel and raises it to the -0.75 exponent, moving every lane. clipSize is (1, 1) so only the first of the two writes is in range, and the texel lanes (0.5, 0.25, 0.75, 1.0) are distinct and exact in binary32, so a swapped lane shows as well.

name: read-write-texture-texels-of-r16float-rgba8uint-rgba16sint
rationale: Reads of read_write textures per bound pixel format (the B3 handback's Metal-oracle check of STORAGE_READ_WITHOUT_FORMAT per format; DESIGN D25, D62.5, D68.4). A read_write texture whose format the shader does not declare is a storage image read without a format in Vulkan (shaderStorageImageReadWithoutFormat and the format's STORAGE_READ_WITHOUT_FORMAT feature, or a declared format chosen from the binding); the texel it returns must equal Metal's read bit for bit. This case binds r16_float to the float texture 0, rgba8_uint to the uint texture 1 and rgba16_sint to the int texture 2, each 16x1. Lane t reads texel (t, 0) of each and stores the raw bits (as_type<uint4> of the float and int texels, the uint texel as is) to out[3t], out[3t+1] and out[3t+2] of buffer 0; the kernel writes no texture (the textures are in_out because a read_write texture is a storage image whose bound format the case supplies as its storage specialization; they are not observed). Texel values: r16_float: +0, -0, 1, -1, +-65504, +-inf, the quiet NaN 0x7e00, the smallest and largest positive half denormals (0x0001, 0x03ff), a negative denormal (0x8001), the smallest normal, 0x3555, 0.5 and the denormal 0x0200: a read that flushes half denormals, as the engine's OpQuantizeToF16 under F16DenormFlush may (DESIGN D68.4), returns a signed zero for the four denormals; rgba8_uint: 64 codes including 0, 1, 128 and 255 (zero-extended); rgba16_sint: 64 codes including -32768, -1, 0 and 32767 (sign-extended to 32 bits). Channels a format lacks are filled by the device (Vulkan fills green and blue with 0 and alpha with 1); the observation records Metal's fill. All three formats are in Metal's tier-2 read_write set, so the reads are defined. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB so an unwritten word is visible; each lane writes only its own three uint4s; the AIR has no loop.

name: float-denormals-in-vector-arithmetic-comparisons-and-functions
rationale: Thread i reads the float vectors (a, b, c) and the int vector n from in[4i .. 4i + 3] and writes 64 words, each row lane-wise: a + b, a - b, a * b, fma(a, b, c), a * b + c, the six comparisons of a and b as bits (<, <=, ==, !=, >, >= at bits 0 to 5), floor(a), ceil(a), sqrt(a), rsqrt(a), ldexp(a, n), (a * b) * c, float(n) * a - c, the comparisons a * b < c, -a < b and fabs(a) == b as bits 0 to 2, fmin(a, b) * c, and step(a, b). Over the 1024 lanes, (a, b) is every pair of a 32-value pool: both zeros, denormals of both signs (the smallest, the largest, others), the smallest normals and their neighbours, values whose products or differences land among the denormals (2^-64, 2^-63, 2^-70, 2^-100, 2^-30, 2^30), and ordinary values; c is the pool at another stride and n runs over -126 to 127. It measures how Metal reads a float denormal operand and flushes a denormal result in vector arithmetic, comparisons, ldexp, sqrt, rsqrt, floor and ceil, and in an operation whose operand is another operation's result (docs/TODO.md 2.2 to 2.5). Compiled without fast math.

name: round-trip-eight-words-through-a-coherent-load-and-store
no_effect: Each lane writes back the word it read coherently, so the answer equals the authored words exactly when every load and store addressed the lane's own element. The write-back is the function's whole effect, so no input makes the answer differ from the authored words: the family has no computing variant.
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.load.system_coherent.volatile.i32.p1i32 (4 case-less corpus sources), which this module pairs with the store form. The MSL that spells system coherence is not reachable from this SDK, and the only other host that calls the load -- `fence_wait` -- spins on it and writes nothing, so `input_coherent` is the one place the load's result reaches memory. What it proves is ADDRESSING, and the case is built for that and claims nothing more: each of the six live lanes reads its own word coherently and writes the same word straight back, so the answer equals the input if and only if every load and every store landed on the lane's own element. The eight words are pairwise distinct and share no byte with each other, so a load shifted by one element, a store shifted by one, a swapped pair or a broadcast all land a word that exists elsewhere in the buffer or nowhere at all. `size` is 6 against a grid of 8, so the last two words are never touched and a lowering that dropped the bound would still have to put them back unchanged -- that part of the module is not observable here, and this case does not pretend to test it.

name: splat-two-motion-vectors-that-round-away-from-zero-both-ways
rationale: The kernel splats a motion vector: it scales each optical-flow vector by one sixteenth, rounds the pair to whole texels, and atomically maxes a packed confidence-and-magnitude word into the splat target at the rounded offset -- once forward from the current flow and once backward from the previous flow. Both vectors were chosen so the rounding lands exactly on a half: 1.5 and 0.5 forward, -0.5 and -1.5 backward, so the case pins that round() goes away from zero in both directions rather than to even, and a shader that rounded to even would splat into (2,0) and (0,0) instead of (2,1) and (1,2). The two destinations also exercise the atomic in both directions: the forward target starts below the incoming word and takes it, and the backward target starts above it and keeps its own, so a max lowered as a plain store would overwrite 0x7F000000. One other case shares a host that calls a texture atomic; this one is authored around the atomic itself rather than reaching it incidentally.

name: escaping-device-and-constant-pointer-integer-differences
rationale: One invocation computes 12- and 28-byte interior-pointer differences in device and constant address spaces, through 64- and 32-bit integer conversions. No pointer-derived address is dereferenced. Input allocations are 32 and 48 bytes. Stores target bytes 8..40 of the 48-byte output, preserving both eight-byte canaries. Expected words are [0xcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcd,12,28,12,28,0xcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcd]. Both source programs have no calls or loops.

name: sobel-gradient-lands-on-a-three-four-five-triangle
rationale: srcOffset and dstOffset are zero and the grid is one thread, so the kernel samples the 2x2 source at normalized coordinate (0, 0) -- texel (0, 0) -- and takes its eight Sobel taps as constant texel offsets around it. Five of those eight leave the texture and clamp_to_edge folds them back onto texels the stencil already reads, so the nine-tap kernel collapses to gy = 3(C - A) + (D - B) and gx = 3(A - B) + (C - D) over the four texels A(0,0), B(1,0), C(0,1) and D(1,1). A and B are zero, leaving gy = 3C + D and gx = C - D. The .x lane's C = 1.75 and D = -1.25 make that (3, 4), and the .y lane's 3.5 and -2.5 make it (6, 8), so air.fast_sqrt.v2f32 is handed the hypotenuse of two Pythagorean triples and has to answer exactly (5, 10). Landing on a perfect square is what makes the fast_ spelling authorable: MoltenVK compiles under MathMode = fast, so a precise:: root would not agree with the Metal oracle, but both run the same fast:: root and 25 and 100 leave it nothing to approximate. Every tap difference and both squares are exact binary32 dyadics, so reassociating either three-term sum under fast math changes no bit. dstLimit is (1, 1), so the in-bounds guard admits exactly this thread, and the constant (0, 1) tail the shader appends keeps the two magnitude lanes distinguishable from each other and from the pair behind them.
